title: Metatables & Metamethods
summary: The mechanism that lets tables customize behavior: __index for fallback lookups (the backbone of OOP), __newindex, __tostring, __add, __eq and friends.

methods.name: setmetatable
methods.description: Assigns mt as t's metatable and returns t (so `setmetatable({}, mt)` is a constructor idiom).

details.heading: Key metamethods
details.body: `__index` — fallback when a key is missing (table or function). `__newindex` — intercepts writes to missing keys. `__tostring` — string form. `__eq`, `__lt`, `__le` — comparisons. `__add`, `__sub`, `__mul`, `__div`, `__unm` — arithmetic. `__call` — makes a table callable like a function. `__iter` (Luau) — custom iteration. `__metatable` — hides the real metatable from getmetatable.

details.heading: __index is the OOP engine
details.body: With `t.__index = t` on a 'class' table and `setmetatable(obj, class)` on instances, method lookups that miss on the instance fall back to the class — that's method inheritance.

explanation.whatItIs: A metatable is a table that describes how *another* table should behave — what happens when a missing key is read, when it's printed, when you add two of them together. Metamethods are the hooks inside it.
explanation.whyItExists: Plain tables are just data. Metatables let you build objects, classes, read-only configs, defaults systems, and vector-like types on top of them.
whenToUse: Defaults: `__index` returns fallback values for missing settings
whenNotToUse: Don't reach for metatables for simple data — plain tables plus functions are clearer
Don't stack clever metamethods where a function call would read fine
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
local class = { greet = function(self) print("hi " .. self.name) end }
class.__index = class          -- "look in class for missing keys"

local obj = setmetatable({ name = "Ada" }, class)
obj:greet()                    -- obj has no `greet`,
                               -- __index redirects to class.greet
```
Read lookup as: 'check the object; if nothing there, ask the metatable's __index where to look.'
tips: Memorize the two-line class idiom: `Class.__index = Class` + `setmetatable(obj, Class)`
Colon calls `obj:method()` pass the object as self — required for instance methods
`table.freeze` is simpler than a read-only metatable for config
commonMistakes: Forgetting `class.__index = class` — methods then never resolve
Using `.` instead of `:` for method calls, so `self` is nil
Expecting metamethods to fire on keys that already exist (they only trigger on misses/writes-to-missing)

examples.title: Defaults via __index
examples.code:
local DEFAULTS = { Speed = 16, Jump = 50, Health = 100 }

local function withDefaults(overrides)
    return setmetatable(overrides or {}, { __index = DEFAULTS })
end

local config = withDefaults({ Speed = 20 })
print(config.Speed)    --> 20  (overridden)
print(config.Jump)     --> 50  (falls back to default)
